title: CedarBridge capacity intake - dedicated vs private tradeoffs
summary: Intro discovery focused on reserved GPU commitment sizing, isolation requirements for multi-tenant inference, burst strategy and fallback to hosted. Customer is evaluating Dedicated for production but needs Private for data residency in EU later. Key concerns: prewarm/warm pool costs, KMS integration, SOC2 audit artifacts, and predictable tail latency at 99.9th percentile.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Head of ML), Ethan Morales (Infra), Sandra Lee (CTO)

Auto-summary: quick discovery. Customer leaning Dedicated but wants Private path later for EU data. Discussed warm pools, prewarm cost tradeoffs, and how Redwood falls back to hosted variants under heavy surge. Also covered KMS and SOC2.

[00:00] Maya Chen: alright hi everyone thanks for joining, um yeah we'll kick off, um quick intros?
[00:08] Priya Nair: hi I'm Priya, Head of ML at CedarBridge, we own model infra and the inference stack, thanks for taking the time.
[00:14] Ethan Morales: Ethan, infra eng, I'll be the one dealing with network/VPC and cost ops.
[00:18] Sandra Lee: Sandra, CTO. We're evaluating dedicated capacity to replace our internal GPU bake cluster.
[00:25] Maya Chen: great, from Redwood we have Liam (SE) and myself. Goal for today is to go over your expected qps/peaks, isolation needs, and timeline. we'll capture next steps.

[00:40] Liam Ortega: quick note, we'll ask a bunch of infra-y q's; feel free to stop me. Starting high level: are you thinking Dedicated reserved pool with burst into hosted or full Private/VPC?
[00:52] Priya Nair: initially reserved Dedicated for predictability, we also have EU-only datasets that will later need Private deployment for residency and compliance. so both paths are on the table.
[01:06] Ethan Morales: yes and we need hard isolation between tenants — multi-tenant on top of company services — so eviction/tenant fencing is a big ask.
[01:16] Maya Chen: understood. Can you share current traffic shape? averages and burst multipliers?
[01:23] Priya Nair: baseline 180 rps average across our core feature endpoints, peak bursts up to ~2.5k rps for short windows (1-3 minutes) during batch scoring. latency SLO target is 95ms p50, 180ms p95, and 350ms p99.9 for single-turn generation.
[01:40] Liam Ortega: thanks. so we're looking at fairly spiky workload. two standard patterns: prewarm/warm pools to reduce cold-start KV cache warmup, or accept fallback to a slightly cheaper hosted variant during burst. both have cost/latency tradeoffs.
[01:54] Ethan Morales: can you explain the warm-pool model — does that mean holding reserved GPUs idle? that seems expensive.
[02:03] Liam Ortega: good question. warm pool or hot nodes are kept in a prewarmed state with KV cache primed for typical prefixes. it reduces first-request latency. you can size the hotpool to cover typical burst magnitude; alternatively, Redwood supports autoscaling with guaranteed reserved capacity for steady-state and burst on top. you pay for reserved GPUs by the commit, but warm-pool size is tunable so you don't keep every GPU hot all the time.
[02:28] Priya Nair: and how does prewarm interact with cost? if we need 100 GPUs all hot, wow that's a lot.
[02:34] Maya Chen: right, that's the economical lever — you choose how many warm nodes vs acceptance of tail latency during surges. Redwood Optimize can suggest a mix given your traffic traces. we'll share a cost model spreadsheet.
[02:48] Sandra Lee: we also have encryption keys managed by our KMS and need HSM/KMS integration for model artifacts and logs. is that supported?
[02:56] Liam Ortega: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. for Hosted/Dedicated we have KMS integrations for keys at rest and can surface audit logs. for Private (VPC/on-prem) we can route everything through your KMS and keep control plane links in your network.
[03:12] Ethan Morales: audit logs — we need immutable audit trails for all inference requests for SOC2 and internal auditing. are those available?
[03:20] Maya Chen: yes, we provide request-level audit logs and per-token cost traces. retention and export can be configured in the Console; for Private deployments we can ship logs to your SIEM.
[03:29] Priya Nair: good. another question: tenancy and noisy neighbor — we have strict isolation requirements for some customers. can we pin workloads to dedicated GPUs?
[03:37] Liam Ortega: yep, you can allocate dedicated pools per tenant or group. Redwood Dedicated supports tenant fencing, node affinity, and segregation policies. we also have resource quotas and preemption policies for lower-tier workloads.
[03:48] Ethan Morales: what's the eviction model? if we hit a surge, do you preempt reserved workloads or will some requests get rerouted to hosted?
[03:56] Liam Ortega: by policy: you can define fallbacks — e.g., on capacity pressure route to a cheaper hosted variant with slightly lower model precision, or throttle non-critical routes. preemption only occurs if you enable cross-tenant preemptions; otherwise, bursts are served by either warm pool or by Redwood's regional routing.
[04:15] Priya Nair: ok policy sounds fine. on the performance side, we also use KV cache heavy workloads with long context windows — 8k tokens typically, sometimes 16k for reports — do you have kernel/quantization optimizations?
[04:28] Liam Ortega: yes, runtime supports attention optimizations and quantization paths; we select kernels based on sequence length. long contexts benefit from tail-optimized kernels and smarter kv cache placement to reduce memory thrash. we also recommend model variants for high-memory contexts.
[04:44] Sandra Lee: anything we should know about GPU types? we currently assume A100 class.
[04:49] Liam Ortega: we support multiple families; Dedicated reservations can be on A10/A100/V100 depending on region and SKU. we can map expected throughput per GPU once we run a baseline with your model.
[04:59] Ethan Morales: can you run a baseline without us shipping model weights? we have IP concerns.
[05:05] Liam Ortega: we can do a perf baseline using a representative model config (same architecture and sequence length) or run tests in a customer-owned Private lab. we don't need your weights for kernel perf; we can approximate.
[05:16] Priya Nair: timeline: we're aiming to have production-ready migration in Q4, with pilot in September. commitment options — monthly vs annual — what are typical pricing/levers?
[05:26] Maya Chen: reserved committed capacity discounts scale with term and GPU count; typical enterprise customers take annual commit for 20-40% off, monthly commits are more flexible but less discount. there are also reserved pool tiers (standard vs isolated). we'll include pricing scenarios.
[05:39] Sandra Lee: about data residency — we need EU-only processing for some datasets starting Nov. can Private be staged after Dedicated?
[05:47] Liam Ortega: yes — many customers do a hybrid approach: Dedicated reserved in region A for steady-state, and later migrate sensitive workloads to Private in EU regions. Redwood's deployment abstraction makes the API consistent. data paths and KMS are configured per deployment.
[06:00] Ethan Morales: on the ops side, do you expose token-level cost breakdowns per route? we want to tie cost to product owners.
[06:07] Maya Chen: yes, Console exposes token-level and route-level metrics, you can tag routes and get per-team billing.
[06:12] Priya Nair: can we enforce rate limits per tenant to avoid blast radius?
[06:16] Liam Ortega: yes, per-tenant quotas and burst tokens are configurable; you can set soft and hard limits with automated throttling.
[06:25] Sandra Lee: what's the SLA? we need 99.9 uptime for inference endpoints.
[06:29] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include the SLA doc. for Private, uptime is co-managed and depends on your infra SLAs.
[06:38] Priya Nair: security review: do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO certs?
[06:42] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and working on ISO; we'll share compliance pack and our security whitepaper.
[06:48] Ethan Morales: ok good. small nit: our infra team needs to see the prewarming eviction math — like how many hot nodes to support a 10x burst for 3 minutes at 99.9. can you help model that?
[06:59] Liam Ortega: yes we can model with your traffic traces. we have a burst-sim script that approximates token-level cost and latency given different hotpool sizes and autoscale thresholds. i'll send it.
[07:10] Priya Nair: also curious about fallback model fidelity — if you route to hosted variant during a storm, will outputs differ materially? our app is sensitive to hallucinations.
[07:21] Liam Ortega: outputs can differ if the hosted model variant is lower-precision or quantized differently. we recommend keeping a canary route and running evals on a small prompt set to measure regression. Redwood Optimize will provide suggestions and regression alerts tied to evals.
[07:36] Sandra Lee: ok let's talk numbers quickly: given 180 rps baseline and 2.5k burst, how many GPUs would you estimate?
[07:44] Liam Ortega: rough ballpark depends on model throughput — assuming X throughput per A100 (we'll get exact), baseline might need 6-8 GPUs steady, and to cover a 2.5k burst you'd either size warmpool to ~25-30 GPUs or accept fallback for peak minutes. again we'll run throughput tests.
[08:02] Ethan Morales: 25-30 GPUs warm seems high cost. is hybrid possible — keep 10 hot and auto-burst to hosted?
[08:08] Maya Chen: absolutely, hybrid is common. you can keep a small hotpool for latency-sensitive core calls and route bulk batch scoring to either scheduled workers or hosted endpoints with acceptable latency.
[08:18] Priya Nair: regarding billing for warmpool — do we pay full reserved rate for hot nodes?
[08:23] Maya Chen: warm nodes are part of reserved capacity; you're billed for reserved capacity committed. cost engineering choices are about how many reserved vs how much to rely on hosted.
[08:33] Sandra Lee: any limits on model size? we run a 70B parameter model for generation.
[08:38] Liam Ortega: 70B is supported on A100-class; memory/perf depends on quantization; for 16k context we may suggest model sharding or a quantized variant to optimize throughput.
[08:49] Ethan Morales: about network/topology for Private: can we route control plane through our VPC?
[08:55] Liam Ortega: yes, Private offers customer-controlled networking and optional on-prem package. control plane links can be over your network and we support peering and private link options.
[09:05] Priya Nair: any references from similar migrations?
[09:08] Maya Chen: we'll share two case studies: one hybrid enterprise and one full Private migration (anonymized).
[09:13] Ethan Morales: ok next steps: we'll provide traffic dumps and target SLOs by Friday. what's the target date for the follow-up?
[09:20] Maya Chen: we proposed Aug 26 for a technical deep dive where Liam will walk your infra team through logs and perf baseline.
[09:26] Sandra Lee: works for us.
[09:29] (brief cross-talk and scheduling)
[09:40] Priya Nair: last question — compliance: if we go Dedicated first then Private later, how is data purged from the Dedicated pool?
[09:48] Liam Ortega: data retention and purge policies can be configured; we provide wipe procedures and attestations for model artifacts and cache. in Dedicated we can configure ephemeral KV and set retention windows.
[09:57] Ethan Morales: great.
[10:00] Maya Chen: ok we'll summarize and send pricing and the perf kit. thanks everyone.

Transcript notes: occasional misrecognitions (eg "K V cash" for KV cache), some speaker turn labels were generic in spotty moments.

End of call.
